name: Times club monthly special crossword No 20,239

solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Rotation of soil by first person in English and French and Mexican community farms

indicators.note: a rotation turns things round, so the whole string that follows is read back to front

blocks.note: sod is turf, the top layer of soil

explanation.surface: A lesson on crop rotation, with first-person pronouns thrown in, about Mexican farmland.
explanation.walkthrough: The rotation covers everything after it: the soil word, then 'I' and its French equivalent, all read backwards together.
explanation.definitionFit: An ejido is a piece of communal land farmed jointly by a village in Mexico, so these are plural holdings of that kind.

clue.text: Younger aged shield-bearer never seeing king or one with regal bearing

indicators.note: never seeing means the named letters go missing from the word before them

blocks.note: abbreviation of junior, the younger of two with one name
an esquire originally carried a knight's shield

explanation.surface: A young knight's squire who has never met the king or anyone of royal bearing.
explanation.walkthrough: ESQUIRE loses R and I to leave ESQUE; JUN, O and ESQUE give JUNOESQUE.
explanation.definitionFit: Junoesque describes a stately, statuesque woman, carrying herself like Juno, queen of the Roman gods.

clue.text: Diameter over velocity plus volume over area in spacetime, say

blocks.note: D for diameter placed above V for velocity, as in a fraction
V for volume placed above A for area

explanation.surface: A physics formula: diameter over velocity added to volume over area, somewhere in spacetime.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue 'over' means placed above, so each symbol simply comes before the next. 'Say' marks spacetime as an example.
explanation.definitionFit: A dvandva is a compound word joining two equal parts, like space plus time, which makes spacetime an example.

clue.text: Step up energy to undermine energy-efficiency indicator

indicators.note: in a down clue, going up means the word is written from bottom to top

blocks.note: pas is a step in dancing
the UK Standard Assessment Procedure rating for homes

explanation.surface: Raising energy levels to defeat an efficiency rating.
explanation.walkthrough: A multiple clue: a reversed dance step, then three meanings of one short word. SAP is the British government's official energy rating for homes.
explanation.definitionFit: Sap as a verb means weaken or erode, and SAP is also the acronym for the standard British home energy-efficiency score.

clue.text: Volk seen going walkabout in this?

definitions.text: Volk seen going walkabout in this?

indicators.note: going walkabout means wandering off, so these letters stray from their order

explanation.surface: South African folk out for a long walk, wearing these.
explanation.walkthrough: Volk is Afrikaans for people, so the whole clue pictures South Africans out walking in the shoe.
explanation.definitionFit: A velskoen is a South African rawhide shoe, just what the people would wear for a long tramp.

clue.text: Poet’s prodigious pen: see answer above

blocks.note: v for vide, Latin for see
a sty is a pen for pigs

explanation.surface: A poet's grand pen, with a footnote pointing to the answer above.
explanation.walkthrough: 'See answer above' looks like a cross-reference; in a down clue it means V and A placed above the pen.
explanation.definitionFit: Vasty is Shakespeare's word for vast or immense, as in 'the vasty deep', so it is a poetic form of huge.

clue.text: Maybe a wash-out celebrity welcomes team by way of note

indicators.note: welcomes means takes in, so the outer word receives the others inside it

blocks.note: a lion is a celebrated person
an eleven, as in a cricket or football side
ti, the seventh note of the scale

explanation.surface: A failed celebrity who lets a sports team in through the back way.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Wash-out' suggests a flop; read literally it is washing something out, which is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Lixiviation is leaching: washing soluble matter out of a solid, so a wash-out is one example.

clue.text: Most of Scots know Dollar stores British cheese there

indicators.note: most of means the word loses its final letter
stores means holds in stock, so one piece is kept inside another

blocks.note: buck is slang for a dollar

explanation.surface: A Scottish shop called Dollar keeps British cheese in stock.
explanation.walkthrough: KE followed by BUCK holds B between them. Dollar is also a town in Scotland, which helps the surface. 'There' refers back to Scotland.
explanation.definitionFit: Kebbuck is a Scots dialect term for a whole round cheese, so it means cheese in Scotland.

clue.text: High priest interrupted by chief ambassador

indicators.note: being interrupted means having something break into the middle

blocks.note: Eli, the high priest in the Book of Samuel
CH is an abbreviation of chief

explanation.surface: A high priest cut short by a chief envoy.
explanation.definitionFit: Elchi is a Turkish and Persian word for an envoy sent by a ruler to a foreign court.

clue.text: Decoration on band twisting middle of knee and wrist

indicators.note: twisting round turns the two letters so they face the other way
middle of keeps only the central letters of the word

blocks.note: carpus is the anatomical name for the wrist

explanation.surface: A decorative band twisted around a knee and wrist.
explanation.walkthrough: The band is architectural: a frieze. The joints point to anatomy, and the wrist's Latin name supplies most of the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: An encarpus is a carved festoon of fruit and flowers used as ornament on a frieze, the band below a cornice.

clue.text: It is about containing breach in odd places in pirate ships of yore

indicators.note: turned about means facing back the other way, so read the word backwards
odd places are positions one, three, five and so on
containing means holding the next piece inside

blocks.note: it is a slang term for sex or sex appeal
the first, third and fifth letters

explanation.surface: Pirate vessels of old, holed and with odd things on board.
explanation.walkthrough: 'It' as sex appeal is a common crossword usage. XES holds BEC to give XEBECS.
explanation.definitionFit: A xebec is a small three-masted Mediterranean vessel, much used by Barbary corsairs in earlier centuries.

clue.text: Chemist’s employees against attention directed to the Left

indicators.note: travelling leftward in an across answer means writing right to left

blocks.note: keep an eye on, pay attention

explanation.surface: A pharmacist's workers opposing attention paid to left-wing politics.
explanation.walkthrough: The 's stands for 'is'. 'Chemist' tempts as a pharmacy, but it is the scientist who devised the periodic table.
explanation.definitionFit: Dmitri Mendeleyev was the Russian scientist who arranged the elements into the periodic table.

clue.text: Numbers busy cutting fruit tree short to reveal low church window

indicators.note: short means cut off at the end, losing a final letter
cutting into means slicing through the middle of something

blocks.note: busy is British slang for a police officer

explanation.surface: Lots of busy work cutting back an orchard tree to uncover a low church window.
explanation.walkthrough: Busy is British slang for a policeman. LYCHE, short of its last E, is cut by NOSCOP.
explanation.definitionFit: A lychnoscope is a small low window in a church chancel wall, sometimes called a low side window.

clue.text: Low-level software returned each of consecutive letters

indicators.note: returned each of means every item is separately turned round

blocks.note: nu and xi follow one another in the Greek alphabet

explanation.surface: Basic computer code that sent back every one of a run of letters.
explanation.walkthrough: The letters are Greek, and each is reversed separately rather than the pair as a whole.
explanation.definitionFit: Unix is an operating system, the core software layer between a computer's hardware and its applications.

clue.text: Second for Cambridge as light blue

indicators.note: second means take the letter in position two

blocks.note: qua means as, in the capacity of

explanation.surface: Cambridge's runner-up in the Boat Race, wearing light blue.
explanation.walkthrough: Light blue is Cambridge University's sporting colour, which disguises the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Aqua is a pale greenish-blue colour, so it names a light shade of blue.

clue.text: For example 13 fire into rabbit fur worn on head

indicators.note: going into something means placed inside it

blocks.note: 13-across is an example of an operating system
rabbit is British slang for chatter or talk

explanation.surface: Firing at a rabbit and wearing its fur as a hat.
explanation.walkthrough: To rabbit on is British slang for to chatter. OSSACK goes into CHAT.
explanation.definitionFit: A Cossack hat is a tall brimless fur hat as worn by the Cossack cavalry of Russia.

clue.text: It’s medium in South Australia, not large in Perth

indicators.note: in means sitting inside the next piece

blocks.note: M for medium, as on clothing sizes
the standard abbreviation of the state

explanation.surface: A clothing size in Australia, compared with Perth.
explanation.walkthrough: Perth looks Australian, but this Perth is the Scottish city, so the answer is a Scots word.
explanation.definitionFit: Sma is the Scots spelling of small, the opposite of large, as said in Scotland.

clue.text: Preserve an opportunity to speak with artist to set up Hindu school

indicators.note: set up in a down clue means raised from bottom to top

explanation.surface: Keeping a chance to speak, alongside an artist, so as to found a Hindu school.
explanation.definitionFit: The Arya Samaj is a Hindu reform movement founded in 1875, a school of thought rooted in the Vedas.

clue.text: Table-cooked food is very soft, some held by wood implements at first

indicators.note: held by means gripped inside the following piece
at first means take just the opening letter

explanation.surface: Food cooked at the table is tender, some of it held in wooden utensils.
explanation.walkthrough: PPANY goes inside TEAK, then the I is added.
explanation.definitionFit: Teppanyaki is Japanese cooking on a hot iron griddle set into the diners' table.

clue.text: Red previously seen in unfinished Gauguin, perhaps

indicators.note: seen in means appearing inside the following piece
unfinished means the final letter is never added

blocks.note: Paul Gauguin's first name, one of many Pauls

explanation.surface: A red colour spotted earlier in an unfinished Gauguin painting.
explanation.walkthrough: Gauguin suggests painting; 'perhaps' tells you he is one example of a Paul. ONCE sits inside PAU.
explanation.definitionFit: Ponceau is a bright poppy red, named from the French word for the corn poppy.

clue.text: Oil lamp in regular use by dairyman

indicators.note: regular means at even intervals, taking every other letter

blocks.note: letters one, three, five and seven

explanation.surface: A farmer with an oil lamp he uses every day in the dairy.
explanation.definitionFit: A diya is a small clay oil lamp lit in South Asia, especially during Diwali.

clue.text: Old maid’s shock, carrying maiden over lake

indicators.note: carrying means holding something within

blocks.note: M for maiden and O for over, cricket scoring abbreviations

explanation.surface: An old maid is shocked when someone carries a young girl across a lake.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Maiden over' is a cricket term, an over with no runs. The 's stands for 'is'. MO goes inside DAZE, then L.
explanation.definitionFit: Damozel is an archaic or poetic form of damsel, meaning a young unmarried woman, as in Rossetti's 'Blessed Damozel'.

clue.text: Egypt’s sunny representative rejected polite but informal refusal

indicators.note: rejected suggests thrown back, so read the phrase backwards

explanation.surface: A sunny Egyptian envoy turned down by someone saying a polite but casual no.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Ta' is British informal for thanks.
explanation.definitionFit: Aton, or Aten, is the disc of the sun worshipped in ancient Egypt, so the god represented the sun.

clue.text: Leaves to chew over accepting the Arabic form of Islamic divorce

indicators.note: over, as in turned over, means reversed
accepting means taking in

blocks.note: qat is a shrub whose leaves are chewed as a stimulant
al is the Arabic definite article

explanation.surface: Mulling over leaves while accepting an Arabic form of divorce.
explanation.walkthrough: AL goes inside QAT after the Q, and the result is read upwards.
explanation.definitionFit: Talaq is the Islamic divorce in which the husband repudiates his wife by declaration.

clue.text: Never failing to include island celebs from S American republic

indicators.note: to include means taking other pieces inside

explanation.surface: Celebrities from an island who always turn up from a South American republic.
explanation.definitionFit: Surinamese means of or relating to Suriname, the small republic on South America's north coast.

clue.text: From country parts of America, Alabama’s plucked down under owls

indicators.note: plucked means pulled out, so these letters are removed

blocks.note: rural US, the countryside of the States

explanation.surface: Birds from rural America, Alabama's plucked, in Australasia.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Down under' points to Australia and New Zealand.
explanation.definitionFit: A ruru is the morepork, a small brown owl native to New Zealand and Australia.

clue.text: Power of reflection: that of verse reduced worthless talk

indicators.note: that stands for the reflection just named, and a reflection is a mirror image
reduced means cut short, losing its last letter

blocks.note: an ode is a lyric poem

explanation.surface: A treatise asking whether poetry or idle talk has more power to make us reflect.
explanation.walkthrough: 'That' borrows the definition's reflection: the mirror image of ODE plus BLA gives ALBEDO.
explanation.definitionFit: Albedo measures how much light a surface such as a planet sends back, its reflecting power.

clue.text: Old-timer’s poem about disheartened alcoholic’s aid for biochemical change

indicators.note: about means placed around the following piece
disheartened means the central letter is taken out

blocks.note: rime is the old spelling of rhyme, as in Coleridge

explanation.surface: An old man's poem about a heartbroken drunk, mixed with talk of biochemistry.
explanation.walkthrough: BOOZY loses its middle O, and RIME goes round the rest.
explanation.definitionFit: A ribozyme is an RNA molecule that acts as an enzyme, catalysing chemical reactions in cells.

clue.text: Oscar bagged by monochrome film’s sex symbol

indicators.note: bagged by means caught and held inside

explanation.surface: A black-and-white film's sex symbol wins an Oscar.
explanation.walkthrough: Oscar looks like the film award but is just the letter O.
explanation.definitionFit: Clara Bow was the silent-film star known as the 'It girl', Hollywood's leading sex symbol of the 1920s.

clue.text: Group of stars people generally put on uniform after sailor changes into uniform

indicators.note: changes into means one element is swapped for another
put on means placed after what precedes it, so this piece comes last
after tells us the swap happens once the uniform word is in place, sending that piece second

explanation.surface: Ordinary folk getting into uniform after a sailor changes into his.
explanation.walkthrough: AB inside EQUABLE is replaced by U to make EQUULE, which is followed by US.
explanation.definitionFit: Equuleus, the Little Horse, is a small constellation in the northern sky, near Pegasus.

clue.text: Art going to get stuck briefly in outback shelter

indicators.note: briefly means cut short, dropping the last letter

blocks.note: 'thou art going to' is the old 'thou wilt'
to jam is to get stuck

explanation.surface: Art that is about to jam, briefly stuck in an outback shelter.
explanation.walkthrough: Art is the archaic 'thou art', and 'thou wilt' means you are going to.
explanation.definitionFit: A wiltja is an Aboriginal shelter or windbreak made of branches in the Australian outback.
